facts.text: McGees Mills earned its name from a gristmill run by Henry Holmes McGee, whose milling operation gave the community its identity.
The town’s founding dates back to 1826, when itinerant Methodist minister James McGee established a sawmill and gristmill along the West Branch of the Susquehanna River.
In 1873, builders completed the McGees Mills Covered Bridge, the last covered bridge spanning the West Branch Susquehanna and the only one in Clearfield County.
The Bell's Gap Railroad reached McGees Mills in 1887, with a station opening by 1893 and linking the village to coal and lumber markets via the Clearfield and Jefferson Railway.
McGees Mills sits at the junction of U.S. Route 219 and Pennsylvania Route 36, about two miles west‑northwest of Mahaffey.
Today the village preserves its 19th‑century layout, with frame houses and the historic bridge framing a scenic river backdrop that echoes the era of Pennsylvania lumber.
